prompt:
Consider the following company information, reported as of 2026-02-24. Act as a credit rating analyst.
| Current ratio           | 0.53 |
| Retained earnings       | -12,237M |
| Current liabilities     | 6,106M |
| Current assets          | 3,244M |
| Shareholders' equity    | 12,807M |
| Total liabilities       | 43,578M |
| Total assets            | 58,573M |
| EBIT / operating income | 1,307M |
| Revenue                 | 3,198M |
Based only on the above and knowledge predating 2026-02-24, assign the issuer a letter credit rating on the 21-grade scale below (finest granularity you can justify). Choose exactly one label from: AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-, CC, C.
Reason briefly in 1-3 sentences. Then, on a separate final line, output exactly:
DECISION: <one label>
raw_response:
The reported metrics indicate a highly leveraged capital structure (total liabilities ~74% of assets) with negative working capital and a large accumulated deficit, all consistent with an issuer that has experienced material financial distress and carries a substantial risk of default. Positive (but narrow) operating income provides limited offset and does not support an investment-grade or upper-speculative-grade rating.

DECISION: CCC

(The rating is placed at CCC rather than B or CC because the balance-sheet and liquidity metrics are unambiguously weak while the firm is still generating positive EBIT and has not yet shown an imminent payment default.)
